summary: Two paragraph-specific gaps justify a small retrieval pass for Open LLM Leaderboard benchmark context and direct Rasch/IRT foundations; the existing related-work coverage needs no expansion.

rewrite_targets.reason: The opening benchmark paragraph names four Open LLM Leaderboard-derived cases without a direct reference to that collection, and the bibliography contains no dedicated Leaderboard source. Liang2023 already supplies HELM context and can be reused locally without retrieval. One authoritative Leaderboard collection reference would identify the upstream evaluation context; it must not be used to substantiate the staged case counts, exact snapshot, filtering, or benchmark-version equivalence, which remain artifact-grounded.
rewrite_targets.anchor_text: four Open LLM Leaderboard-derived cases (BBH, GPQA, MuSR, and OpenLLM Math)
search_topics: Open LLM Leaderboard benchmark collection documentation BBH GPQA MuSR OpenLLM Math

rewrite_targets.reason: The reconstruction paragraph introduces a Rasch response model without a direct foundational citation. Related Work cites Andersen1970 specifically to distinguish conditional maximum-likelihood estimation, not to explain the response-model family; its stored abstract concerns conditional estimation. The later local comparator uses a two-parameter logistic model and fitted item information, also without a direct foundational reference. One or two authoritative IRT sources could support these named model families and their distinction without implying that the custom fitting procedure is standard, that the local comparator reproduces a published system, or that the profile branch has an established empirical benefit.
rewrite_targets.anchor_text: The nonlinear branch retains source response profiles while smoothing them with a Rasch model.
